questions.stem: For a notebook problem, 11 - How many edges does the complete graph K_11 have?

options.misconception: it counts ordered pairs instead of unordered edges
it uses a power of two instead of a binomial coefficient
it omits one connecting edge

questions.explanation: In a complete graph every pair of the 11 vertices is joined by exactly one edge, so the number of edges is C(11,2) which equals 55. Choice B is a distractor: it counts ordered pairs instead of unordered edges. Choice C is a distractor: it uses a power of two instead of a binomial coefficient. Choice D is a distractor: it omits one connecting edge.
questions.hint: Count unordered pairs of vertices.

questions.stem: In a problem-solving set, 9 - A graph has 9 edges. What is the sum of the degrees of all its vertices?

options.misconception: it counts each edge only once
it halves instead of doubles
it counts each edge four times

questions.explanation: By the handshaking lemma, every edge contributes 2 to the total degree, so a graph with 9 edges has total degree 18. Choice B is a distractor: it counts each edge only once. Choice C is a distractor: it halves instead of doubles. Choice D is a distractor: it counts each edge four times.
questions.hint: Each edge touches two vertices, so it adds two to the degree sum.
